_commentaire: Référentiel daté d'oracle-scan-workflow-agent (TF-2002) : les actions et commandes qui lancent un agent dans un workflow GitHub Actions, les événements qu'un tiers déclenche, et les faits de documentation qui fondent les règles WA-1 à WA-7. Donnée volatile (loi n° 4) : une action renommée ou une option nouvelle se corrige ici.

commandes_agent.agent: Claude Code en ligne de commande

citations: The action can only be triggered by users with write access to the repository.
This is a significant security risk and should only be used for workflows with extremely limited permissions
Should be used with extreme caution as it bypasses the primary security mechanism of this action
If your workflow listens on those events and `allowed_bots` is set to `'*'`, any such App can invoke this action with a prompt it controls.

Write access: on issue and pull request events, the triggering user must have write access to the repository. To allow specific users without write access, set allowed_non_write_users and pass your own github_token input.
Invoking Copilot CLI directly in workflow steps gives it broad access to your workflow environment.
copilot -p "Use git show HEAD to summarize the changes in this commit" -s --allow-tool='shell(git show:*)'
Workflows that run on pull request events from forks are at higher risk of prompt injection.
These contexts typically end with body, default_branch, email, head_ref, label, message, name, page_name, ref, and title.
Before the shell script is run, the expressions inside ${{ }} are evaluated and then substituted with the resulting values
The action sanitizes content by stripping HTML comments, invisible characters, markdown image alt text, hidden HTML attributes, and HTML entities, but new bypass techniques may emerge.
When set, Claude does a best-effort scrub of Anthropic, cloud, and GitHub Actions secrets from subprocess environments.
This reduces but does not eliminate prompt injection risk

pull_request_target and workflow_run execute with the base repository's secrets.
Do not check out an untrusted ref into the workspace root before this action.
For a plain-text prompt, Claude has no shell or GitHub API access until you grant the tools the prompt needs, with --allowedTools in claude_args or a permissions.allow rule in the settings input.
id-token: write: required for the Claude Code GitHub Action's default GitHub App authentication
The job MUST be called copilot-setup-steps or it will not be picked up by Copilot.
Set the permissions to the lowest permissions possible needed for your steps.
Copilot will be given its own token for its operations.
